ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The large rectangle in the figure is divided into three horizontal regions: the topmost one has 2 congruent small rectangles placed horizontally, the middle one has 5 congruent small rectangles placed vertically, and the bottommost one also has 2 congruent small rectangles placed horizontally. All small rectangles are the same size. Reasoning: Let the long side of each small rectangle be 10 cm, and the short side be x cm. It can be seen from the figure that the total width of the large rectangle is both equal to the sum of the long sides of the 2 horizontally placed small rectangles above, and also equal to the sum of the short sides of the 5 vertically placed small rectangles in the middle, so 2×10=5x, giving x=4. The width of the large rectangle is 20 cm, and its height is the upper short side 4 cm + the middle long side 10 cm + the lower short side 4 cm, namely 18 cm. Therefore the perimeter is 2×(20+18)=76 cm.

Let each small rectangle have long side 10 cm and short side x cm. From the image, the total width of the large rectangle is both 2 long sides across the top row and 5 short sides across the middle row, so 2·10 = 5x, giving x = 4. Then the large rectangle has width 20 and height x + 10 + x = 18. Its perimeter is 2(20 + 18) = 76 cm.
